# Astarte.Core.CQLUtils

Source: https://astarte-core.hexdocs.pm/Astarte.Core.CQLUtils.md

# `Astarte.Core.CQLUtils`
[🔗](https://github.com/astarte-platform/astarte_core/blob/main/lib/astarte_core/cql_utils.ex#L19)

This module contains a set of functions that should be used to map Astarte types and concepts to C*

# `endpoint_id`
[🔗](https://github.com/astarte-platform/astarte_core/blob/main/lib/astarte_core/cql_utils.ex#L157)

returns an endpoint UUID for a certain `endpoint` on a certain `interface_name` with a certain `interface_major`.

# `endpoint_to_db_column_name`
[🔗](https://github.com/astarte-platform/astarte_core/blob/main/lib/astarte_core/cql_utils.ex#L61)

Returns the column name for a certain endpoint that will be used for object interface tables.

# `interface_descriptor_statement`
[🔗](https://github.com/astarte-platform/astarte_core/blob/main/lib/astarte_core/cql_utils.ex#L94)

Returns the CQL query statement that should be used to retrieve interface descriptor from the database.

# `interface_id`
[🔗](https://github.com/astarte-platform/astarte_core/blob/main/lib/astarte_core/cql_utils.ex#L145)

Returns interface UUID for a certain `interface_name` with a certain `interface_major`

# `interface_name_to_table_name`
[🔗](https://github.com/astarte-platform/astarte_core/blob/main/lib/astarte_core/cql_utils.ex#L33)

Returns a generated table name that might be used during table creation."

# `is_valid_cql_name?`
[🔗](https://github.com/astarte-platform/astarte_core/blob/main/lib/astarte_core/cql_utils.ex#L87)

Returns true if a given CQL name can be safely used for a table or a column name

# `mapping_value_type_to_db_type`
[🔗](https://github.com/astarte-platform/astarte_core/blob/main/lib/astarte_core/cql_utils.ex#L101)

Returns a CQL type for a given mapping value type atom

# `realm_name_to_keyspace_name`
[🔗](https://github.com/astarte-platform/astarte_core/blob/main/lib/astarte_core/cql_utils.ex#L172)

```elixir
@spec realm_name_to_keyspace_name(nonempty_binary(), binary()) :: nonempty_binary()
```

# `type_to_db_column_name`
[🔗](https://github.com/astarte-platform/astarte_core/blob/main/lib/astarte_core/cql_utils.ex#L123)

Returns table column name that stores a certain type.

---

*Consult [api-reference.md](api-reference.md) for complete listing*

# Astarte.Core.Device

Source: https://astarte-core.hexdocs.pm/Astarte.Core.Device.md

# `Astarte.Core.Device`
[🔗](https://github.com/astarte-platform/astarte_core/blob/main/lib/astarte_core/device.ex#L19)

Utility functions to deal with Astarte devices

# `device_id`
[🔗](https://github.com/astarte-platform/astarte_core/blob/main/lib/astarte_core/device.ex#L24)

```elixir
@type device_id() :: &lt;&lt;_::128&gt;&gt;
```

# `encoded_device_id`
[🔗](https://github.com/astarte-platform/astarte_core/blob/main/lib/astarte_core/device.ex#L25)

```elixir
@type encoded_device_id() :: String.t()
```

# `decode_device_id`
[🔗](https://github.com/astarte-platform/astarte_core/blob/main/lib/astarte_core/device.ex#L39)

```elixir
@spec decode_device_id(encoded_device_id :: encoded_device_id(), opts :: options) ::
  {:ok, device_id :: device_id()} | {:error, atom()}
when options: [option], option: {:allow_extended_id, boolean()}
```

Decodes a Base64 url encoded device id and returns it as a 128-bit binary (usable as uuid).

By default, it will fail with `{:error, :extended_id_not_allowed}` if the size of the encoded device_id is > 128 bit.
You can pass `allow_extended_id: true` as second argument to allow longer device ids (the returned binary will still be 128 bit long, but the function will not return an error and will instead drop the extended id).

Returns `{:ok, device_id}` or `{:error, reason}`.

# `decode_extended_device_id`
[🔗](https://github.com/astarte-platform/astarte_core/blob/main/lib/astarte_core/device.ex#L59)

```elixir
@spec decode_extended_device_id(encoded_device_id :: encoded_device_id()) ::
  {:ok, device_id :: device_id(), extended_id :: binary()} | {:error, atom()}
```

Decodes an extended Base64 url encoded device id.

Returns `{:ok, device_id, extended_id}` (where `device_id` is a binary with the first 128 bits of the decoded id and `extended_id` the rest of the decoded binary) or `{:error, reason}`.

# `encode_device_id`
[🔗](https://github.com/astarte-platform/astarte_core/blob/main/lib/astarte_core/device.ex#L75)

```elixir
@spec encode_device_id(device_id :: device_id()) ::
  encoded_device_id :: encoded_device_id()
```

Encodes a device id with the standard encoding (Base64 url encoding, no padding). The device id must be exactly 16 bytes (128 bits) long.

Returns the encoded device id.

# `random_device_id`
[🔗](https://github.com/astarte-platform/astarte_core/blob/main/lib/astarte_core/device.ex#L85)

```elixir
@spec random_device_id() :: device_id :: device_id()
```

Generate a random Astarte device id.

The generated device id is also a valid UUID v4.

# `valid_name?`
[🔗](https://github.com/astarte-platform/astarte_core/blob/main/lib/astarte_core/group.ex#L29)

Valid group names _do not_ start with reserved characters `@` and `~`.

@type t() :: %Astarte.Core.InterfaceDescriptor{

  major_version: non_neg_integer(),
  minor_version: non_neg_integer(),

  ownership: Astarte.Core.Interface.Ownership.t() | nil,

# `from_db_result`
[🔗](https://github.com/astarte-platform/astarte_core/blob/main/lib/astarte_core/interface_descriptor.ex#L49)

Deserializes an `%InterfaceDescriptor{}` from `db_result`.
`db_result` can be a keyword list or a map.

Returns the `{:ok, %InterfaceDescriptor{}}` on success,
`{:error, :invalid_interface_descriptor_data}` on failure.

# `from_db_result!`
[🔗](https://github.com/astarte-platform/astarte_core/blob/main/lib/astarte_core/interface_descriptor.ex#L98)

Deserializes an `%InterfaceDescriptor{}` from `db_result`.
`db_result` can be a keyword list or a map.

Returns the `%InterfaceDescriptor{}` on success,
raises on failure

# `from_interface`
[🔗](https://github.com/astarte-platform/astarte_core/blob/main/lib/astarte_core/interface_descriptor.ex#L112)

Builds an `%InterfaceDescriptor{}` starting from an `%Interface{}`

Returns the `%InterfaceDescriptor{}`

# Astarte.Core.Mapping.EndpointsAutomaton

Source: https://astarte-core.hexdocs.pm/Astarte.Core.Mapping.EndpointsAutomaton.md

# `Astarte.Core.Mapping.EndpointsAutomaton`
[🔗](https://github.com/astarte-platform/astarte_core/blob/main/lib/astarte_core/mapping/endpoints_automaton.ex#L19)

# `build`
[🔗](https://github.com/astarte-platform/astarte_core/blob/main/lib/astarte_core/mapping/endpoints_automaton.ex#L53)

builds the automaton for given `mappings`, returns `:ok` followed by the automaton tuple if build succeeded, otherwise `:error` and the reason.

# `is_valid?`
[🔗](https://github.com/astarte-platform/astarte_core/blob/main/lib/astarte_core/mapping/endpoints_automaton.ex#L66)

returns true if `nfa` is valid for given `mappings`

# `lint`
[🔗](https://github.com/astarte-platform/astarte_core/blob/main/lib/astarte_core/mapping/endpoints_automaton.ex#L75)

returns a list of likely invalid endpoints for a certain list of `mappings`.

# `parse_endpoint`
[🔗](https://github.com/astarte-platform/astarte_core/blob/main/lib/astarte_core/mapping/endpoints_automaton.ex#L152)

# `resolve_path`
[🔗](https://github.com/astarte-platform/astarte_core/blob/main/lib/astarte_core/mapping/endpoints_automaton.ex#L26)

returns `:ok` and an endpoint for a given `path` using a previously built automata (`{transitions, accepting_states}`).
if path is not complete one or more endpoints will be guessed and `:guessed` followed by a list of endpoints is returned.

---

# Astarte.Core.Mapping.ValueType

Source: https://astarte-core.hexdocs.pm/Astarte.Core.Mapping.ValueType.md

# `Astarte.Core.Mapping.ValueType`
[🔗](https://github.com/astarte-platform/astarte_core/blob/main/lib/astarte_core/mapping/value_type.ex#L19)

# `t`
[🔗](https://github.com/astarte-platform/astarte_core/blob/main/lib/astarte_core/mapping/value_type.ex#L22)

```elixir
@type t() ::
  :double
  | :integer
  | :boolean
  | :longinteger
  | :string
  | :binaryblob
  | :datetime
  | :doublearray
  | :integerarray
  | :booleanarray
  | :longintegerarray
  | :stringarray
  | :binaryblobarray
  | :datetimearray
```

# Astarte.Core.Realm

Source: https://astarte-core.hexdocs.pm/Astarte.Core.Realm.md

# `Astarte.Core.Realm`
[🔗](https://github.com/astarte-platform/astarte_core/blob/main/lib/astarte_core/realm.ex#L19)

Functions that deal with Astarte realms

# `valid_name?`
[🔗](https://github.com/astarte-platform/astarte_core/blob/main/lib/astarte_core/realm.ex#L32)

Returns true if `realm_name` is a valid realm name, false otherwise.

Valid realm names match this regular expression: `~r/^[a-z][a-z0-9]{0,47}$/`.
In addition, the `astarte` and `system` names and the `system_` prefix are reserved.

---

*Consult [api-reference.md](api-reference.md) for complete listing*

[🔗](https://github.com/astarte-platform/astarte_core/blob/main/lib/astarte_core/triggers/policy/policy.ex#L118)

# `from_policy_proto!`
[🔗](https://github.com/astarte-platform/astarte_core/blob/main/lib/astarte_core/triggers/policy/policy.ex#L154)

Creates a `Policy` from a `PolicyProto`.

Returns the `%Policy{}` on success,
raises on failure

[🔗](https://github.com/astarte-platform/astarte_core/blob/main/lib/astarte_core/triggers/policy/policy.ex#L170)

It is assumed that the `Policy` is valid and constructed using `Policy.changeset`

Returns a `%PolicyProto{}`
